body:
Fixed and published in [Gaoxy v0.12.2](https://github.com/gsmlg-dev/gaoxy/releases/tag/v0.12.2), source `55ed97d2b05ba2a8dd7c911472833e71dd6b87f7` on `main`.

Socket identity lookup now returns errors instead of raising. The HTTP/1 caller closes normally for `:closed`, `:einval` and `:enotconn` before endpoint dispatch; unexpected errors retain their error disposition. Monitored-owner admission cleanup and successful metadata/deadlines remain intact.

Verification completed:
- Original controlled reproduction: 7 tests / 5 failures before the fix, followed by the same 7 tests / 0 failures.
- Two synchronized real TCP cases observe actual `:enotconn` before exchange creation, then normal owner termination, no exception or endpoint dispatch, admission cleanup, a healthy sibling and a fresh healthy request. Header-only and short-body inputs use `request_timeout: :infinity`.
- Canonical ordinary gate: 466 executed, zero failures/excluded/skipped. All 10 required source CI jobs passed; guarded [release qualification](https://github.com/gsmlg-dev/gaoxy/actions/runs/39803249750) passed on the exact source.
- A separate fresh Hex-only 0.12.2 consumer passed all 9 new regressions, with both real TCP cases again observing `:enotconn`. The two changed published source files match the commit byte for byte.
- All 8 GitHub assets, 7 payload checksums and 6 unretired public Hex distributions verified. All 135 packaged Elixir source files match the publication commit. The initial standalone transfer timed out; its failed receipt is preserved separately from the resumed download and completed full verification.

The downstream storage application's own suite was not run here. The released fix covers Gaoxy's ordinary peer-close handling.
